LEARN VOID / TOOLING & INTEGRATION

Editor tooling & diagnostics

Keep feedback close to the code you wrote.

Illustrative function fragment. Use reading_total(reading, count) as a small source-navigation target: its declaration names both parameters and its return type. This function returns their product; it does not assert that a particular completion or hover UI is already distributed.

Understand source, not backend machinery

VOID’s diagnostic direction is clear .void locations, useful ranges and explanations that refer to language concepts. Normal errors should not require understanding generated LLVM IR, mangled symbols or linker internals.

One language service

The shared language server uses compiler-owned analysis for diagnostics and navigation. Implemented queries include completion, hover, signature help, symbols and guarded editing operations across editor integrations. These capabilities are still in development, with no public editor builds distributed here.

Edits need semantic boundaries

Rename and formatting deliberately operate on supported cases. Rename is not a universal operation on every declaration kind. Formatting is conservative rather than a full reflow or import-sorting system. Semantic highlighting and general code actions are not promised by the current server.

The experience being built

The goal is a useful everyday editor: quick answers about types and parameters, navigation that follows actual declarations, and feedback that stays attached to current source. Package discovery belongs to the future ecosystem; a native package manager is not available.

Source-aware assistance, shared across editors

Completion, documentation hover, parameter help, definitions, references, document/workspace symbols, guarded rename and conservative formatting are implemented through compiler-owned analysis. Module completion follows the selected source graph, including nested import paths. ## documentation comments and ## @param descriptions supply authored help. References inside string interpolation retain their source locations.

VS Code and Neovim provide adapters for the shared server; Vim uses yegappan/lsp with rename disabled. Existing integrations have local Linux execution evidence. VSCodium is a compatibility target with execution unverified; the newest language assistance still needs fresh interactive-client validation. Broader Windows/macOS combinations and clean-machine distribution remain unverified. Installed standard sources are protected from rename and formatting.
